analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: LOWEST VOLUME SESSION YTD
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -6bps at 7,807 with a $3Bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX fell 71bps to 30,664, R2K fell 41bps to 2,795, and the Dow rose 38bps to 51,850.

Volume was the lowest of the year: 12.65bn shares traded across US exchanges vs a YTD daily average of 18.577bn. Exchange volumes were 20.7% below the 20-day average. GS attributes this to the holiday and sparse news.

Semis were weak, led by Memory. Drivers cited: China memory progress, follow-through from Korea (KOSPI -365bps), and an ongoing turn in flows. The GS desk was much better for sale across memory and HDDs into the end of last week.
Mag7 continued to trade firm. META rose 4% on the introduction of 'Muse Wonder', alongside an ongoing 'flight to quality' rotation.
Crude moved higher on weekend escalations in the Middle East. WTI rose 152bps to $93.25.
The GS floor rated overall activity a 2 on a 1-10 scale, with client skews benign.

Week ahead: CPI on Wednesday is the main event, with consensus at 0.6% headline and 0.2% core. A 10bp downside surprise on core would be meaningful for rates. Banks report from Tuesday, ASML Wednesday, TSMC Thursday, plus PPI and retail sales, then Warsh on Friday.

The S&P implied move through Friday's close was about 1% last week and about 96bps as of this morning. GS says this is one of the lowest 1-week implied moves in roughly 6 years, despite earnings, CPI and Fed speakers this week.
Flow: clients turned to HYG downside with the bond market closed. 50k Jan 77/73 put spreads were bought, within nearly 300k total options traded today.

GS vol desk sees S&P upside as cheap into month-end given a lack of conviction, low sentiment and narrow breadth. It prefers owning 30 Oct SPY/QQQ gamma for earnings exposure without midterm premium, while still capturing the Fed and the 65% of S&P market cap that reports. The S&P implied move for tomorrow is 34bps.
